4852-history-of-the-united-netherlands-1:
Leicester's return to England in late 1586 shifts the scene to Elizabeth's court, and John Lothrop Motley follows the quarrel that follows him. The trial of Mary, Queen of Scots, leaves the court fearful and divided, while Dutch envoys face the queen's bitter complaints about Leicester and her refusal to spend freely on the war.

Burghley and Davison counsel patience, and a sharp letter from the States in February deepens the rift. Motley presents Elizabeth as shrewd, stubborn, and parsimonious all at once, and the envoys as men caught between a needy republic and a wary queen. It is diplomacy under strain, told through letters and audiences.
history-of-the-united-netherlands-1587b:
John Lothrop Motley covers Leicester's English winter in chapters fourteen and fifteen of his History of the United Netherlands. Leicester is in England, and the trial of the Queen of Scots fills the air. Lord Buckhurst is sent to the Netherlands in his place. He finds an alarming state of affairs on his arrival.

Buckhurst tries conciliation where Leicester ruled by faction. Clerk Wilkes argues democratic theories; Barneveld answers for the States and religious tolerance. Deventer's bad counsels poison Leicester from afar. Elizabeth, angry and vindictive, censures her own envoy's course. Motley quotes Buckhurst's eloquent appeals to the Queen at length. The chapters show a republic surviving its protectors: Dutch statesmen learn to govern while England's court contradicts itself in despatch after despatch.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1437b:
Section 1437b of Title 2 of the United States Code covers support for covered staff who work outside the Washington area. It sits in Chapter 24 of that title, the Congressional Accountability Act, among its general provisions. Part (a) states the rule in general terms. All covered staff whose place of work lies outside the Washington, DC area are to have fair access to aid.

That access covers the resources and services given by the Office and under the chapter. It must match the access given to covered staff who work in the Washington area. Part (b) of the section takes up the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights in this regard. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
uslaw-usc-t2-s907b:
Section 907b of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with a change to an order of the President. It sits in Chapter 20, on powers for times of need to cut budget gaps. A first clause deals with the start of a joint resolution. At any time past the point when the Director of the budget office gives a last report on cuts for a year, a step is let through. The head of the majority in either House may bring in a joint resolution.

That step must fall before the close of the twentieth day of the session that starts past the date of the report. The resolution is to hold rules that tell the President to change the last order made under a named section. It may also give a second path to cut the gap for that year.
